title: Moving Objects
standard_code: Grade 3, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Objects move when they are pushed or pulled. A push or pull can make an object start moving, stop, go faster or slower, or change direction. The speed and direction of objects can be observed and compared. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 3, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): pushes and pulls, strong and gentle forces, speed and direction, and rolling and sliding. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A push or a pull makes things move.
key_sub: A bigger push makes things move farther and faster.
body_html:
How to think about it

A push moves something away from you; a pull moves something toward you. Pushes and pulls are forces. A force can make an object start moving, stop, speed up, slow down or change direction.

A strong push makes a ball roll faster and farther than a gentle push. Round objects roll; flat objects slide. A rough floor slows things down more than a smooth floor.

Example

You open a drawer. Is it a push or a pull?

It comes toward you.

Answer: a pull

Example

How can you make a toy car go farther?

Use a bigger force.

Answer: push it harder

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a moving ball needs a push all the time to keep moving.
  • Mixing up push and pull.
  • Thinking heavy objects are always harder to stop than light ones at any speed.
